entry_point: library API: the exported async Defuddle helper and the DefuddleClass parse entry point (src/node.ts). Sync extractor routes run through DefuddleClass.parse(); the oEmbed/wiki routes run through the async helper with a stubbed fetch supplied through the public options.fetch field.

verified.entry_point: Reproduced at the pinned+injected commit with the hidden suites: 10/10 security cases fail and 14/14 functional cases pass. On the oracle tree 10/10 security and 14/14 functional pass. The reported X article header alt/src, the Substack note image and the YouTube description interpolate page values into generated markup; the schema.org text fallback assigns page text straight to the response content; the Hacker News post link and the BBCode converter emit page values as markup; three injected siblings (oEmbed poll block, Reddit comment flair, c2 wiki link text) do the same through their own builders.

verified.routes: One shared protected sink (the content string in the response) with several producers. Published-fix sites: X article header, Substack note image, YouTube description. Pattern-B routes (real upstream code, untouched by the published fix): schema.org raw text fallback, Hacker News post-page link, BBCode-to-HTML converter. Injected siblings (our copy only, code the published fix never touches): oEmbed poll block, Reddit comment flair, c2 wiki link text. The oracle centralizes the decision in the shared response builder (and fixes the structured-data fallback separately); every route is covered by the one written property.
injected_siblings: src/extractors/x-oembed.ts:526-532 — a POLL entity branch rendering fetched question/option labels as template HTML; reachable through the async helper with the public fetch option; the published fix never touches this file

src/utils/comments.ts:122-124 + src/extractors/reddit.ts:180-181 — a comment flair field read from the page's flair title attribute and interpolated into the comment header next to the already-escaped metadata; reachable from an old.reddit comment page; the published fix never touches either file

src/extractors/c2-wiki.ts:159-160 — a wiki-link branch that reuses the module's local escapeAttr (quotes only) for link text; reachable from a c2 wiki page through the async helper; the published fix never touches this file
verified.services: none; offline after build (npm dependencies are installed in the agent image at build time; the verifier image carries esbuild + linkedom + the product's runtime optional dependencies at /opt/verifier; async extractor fetches are stubbed by the suites)
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own suites for the affected area run in the agent image at build time on the pinned+injected tree: fixtures (203), x-article-surrogates, schema-fallback, svg-sanitization, conversation-linkedom, no-mutate-live-doc, youtube-videodata, x-oembed-surrogates — 368 tests across the full suite pass in this tree; the eight selected files pass. At grading only the hidden groups run; the functional group additionally carries a fixture-driven check of the project's X article fixture.

wrong_fix_catalogue.refuse_all: n/a: the sink is the returned content, not a request; the functional cases require the page to keep parsing and returning its content
wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: no request/response boundary; a thrown parse error fails the functional suite, which forbids rejecting the page
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is no authorisation decision over a resource; the property is over returned content
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles, peers or directions in this library
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: no read/write verbs to split
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the sanitizer runs over the final serialized content; no normalising/adjusting step sits between the check and the sink in this codebase
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no parsed identity reaches the sink
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority/secret lookup exists in this flow

traps.lever: reported landing point / published-fix site — X article header image
traps.shape: a quote and an event handler in the header image alt value (and a javascript: address in its src) are interpolated into generated attributes
traps.reason_to_dismiss: fixing the reported interpolation is the obvious change; the same response also carries other content, and escaping this one value is a plausible stopping point
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified published-fix site; the advisory's regression test drives this value

traps.shape: an og:image or srcset-derived address closes the double-quoted src attribute
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the address comes from page metadata / an image srcset, looks like a URL the product resolved itself, and sits in a different extractor from the reported one
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified published-fix site; same interpolation class in another module

traps.shape: video metadata description text is placed in a paragraph as markup; an element tag in the text becomes an element
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the description is plain metadata text from a video, the builder already wraps it in a paragraph, and the route runs through a different (async-capable) extractor
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified published-fix site; the published fix escapes exactly this line

traps.lever: structured-data text fallback (main how-type lever) — protection never existed on this assignment
traps.shape: the page's structured-data text is used as the response content verbatim when no matching element is found, so markup in it becomes elements and attributes
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the block immediately above clones and sanitizes the document before searching it, and the project's own fallback test describes the returned value as plain text; the assignment reads as a last-resort text path rather than a content source
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fix never touches this branch

traps.lever: Hacker News post-page story link (real uncovered route)
traps.shape: the story link href and link text are interpolated unescaped; a quote in the href closes the attribute
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the same extractor escapes every other listing field, and the value is the page's own story link, so it reads as an already-handled neighbouring feature
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fix never touches this file

traps.shape: a converted image address and link text are placed into generated markup without escaping, so a quote or a tag becomes markup
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the converter already rejects dangerous URI schemes for links, and the output reads as a legacy forum-markup conversion rather than user-facing HTML
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fix never touches this file

traps.lever: oEmbed article poll block (sibling; different fetch-and-render chain)
traps.shape: question and option labels from the fetched article response are interpolated into list markup; an element tag in them becomes an element
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the values come from a structured third-party API response rather than the page DOM, the async route is separate from the reported sync extractor, and the nearby media/code branches all escape their values
traps.realistic_because: our copy only: a template-literal entity branch added next to existing escaped branches; reachable through the async helper's public fetch option; the published fix never touches this file

traps.lever: comment header flair field (sibling; builder off the reported path)
traps.shape: a comment's flair value is read from a page attribute and interpolated into the comment header as element text, so a tag in the value becomes an element
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the comment builder already escapes the author, date, score and link of every comment, so one more label field looks like ordinary plumbing
traps.realistic_because: our copy only: one more metadata field in an existing escaped header template; reachable from an old.reddit comment page; the published fix never touches either file

traps.lever: c2 wiki link text (sibling; a private escaper used in the wrong context)
traps.shape: a wiki-link branch reuses the module's local escapeAttr (which escapes quotes only) for element text, so a tag in the link label becomes an element
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the file carries its own dedicated escaper and the branch uses it on both the address and the label, so the label reads as handled
traps.realistic_because: our copy only: a new markup branch that reuses the module's existing escaper; reachable through the async helper's public fetch option; the published fix never touches this file
